samples.summary: No test that a merge lying entirely past the freeze line leaves the line alone (the sweep's `start > snapped` guard/`break` is untested)
samples.evidence: The rewritten `snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:234-237) grows the line only when `start(range) <= snapped`, and breaks out once a block starts past the line. Every freeze test in merge.test.ts uses blocks that straddle or sit inside the frozen band: 787 (A2:A4 straddling, sole merge), 815 (block ends exactly at the line), 833/860/879 (straddling), 895/911 (cascading chain where every block starts at or before the line). None has a merge that begins strictly below/right of the freeze line, so an implementation that dropped the start-check (or the break) and snapped to any block ending past the line would still pass the whole suite — while a user freezing row 2 on a sheet with an unrelated merge at row 50 would silently get 50 frozen rows.
searchedFor: grep snapFreezePastMerges across packages (no dedicated unit test file for merging.ts)

samples.summary: Column-axis sweep has no cascade/ordering test; the sort is only proven on the row axis
samples.evidence: The delta added `should cascade the snap whatever order the blocks were merged in` (merge.test.ts:911) only for rows. The column branch (`sweep(frozenCols, r=>r[0].c, r=>r[1].c)`, merging.ts:247-251) is exercised only by merge.test.ts:879, a single-block straddle, which cannot detect a missing/incorrect sort on that axis (e.g. if only the row sweep were sorted, or the column comparator compared the wrong field while the growth accessors were right). A column freeze on a chain of merges created out of order would then under-snap and leave a block straddling the boundary — the exact unpaintable state this code exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The stated motivation (quadratic -> single sorted sweep, DoS avoidance) has no test over a large merge map
samples.evidence: The doc comment at merging.ts:199-210 and the backend cap comment at worksheet-settings.ts justify the rewrite by cost on large merge maps (up to the new 10,000-entry ceiling), yet no test feeds `snapFreezePastMerges` more than two merges — there is no direct unit test of the exported function anywhere (grep for `snapFreezePastMerges` matches only src files, index.ts and backend callers). Nothing would catch a future change that reintroduced the fixpoint loop.

samples.summary: The new merge-count ceiling is tested only at the validator; no test covers documents that already exceed it, or other write paths
samples.evidence: `worksheet-settings.spec.ts:114-124` is a genuine, non-vacuous test of `MaxMergeEntries` (10001 rejected, 10000 accepted). But nothing tests that a worksheet already holding more than 10,000 merges (written before this cap, or by a non-`parseMerges` path such as document copy / template / shape migration — see packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts and worksheet-shape-migration.spec.ts, neither of which asserts a merge count) still loads and can still be edited, nor that those other writers enforce the same ceiling. If the cap is enforced only on one door, the guard's effectiveness is untested where it matters.
